chapter: Starting out in New York and Chicago
title: Taking the band to New York: Savoy, Dunbar Palace, Chick Webb
summary: After graduating Horace was offered New York work near Fletcher and played the Savoy Ballroom next to Chick Webb and the Dunbar Palace. Banjoist Talcott Reeves and the McCord brothers came with him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Right after you graduated, then, you had this band still going.

Yes. I had been offered a job in New York to link up with my brother, because there were a couple of clubs there during the Summer that I used to frequent, you know. The Savoy Ballroom, and a place called the Dunbar Palace, (inaudible), and when I graduated, I -- these are some of the jobs that I played.
In the city. In New York City.
In New York City -- the Savoy Ballroom. In fact, I had the honor of being right next on the bandstand to the late great Chick Webb.

Right. Fine. Then, did you -- when you took the band to New York from Wilberforce, did most all of the players that had been working with you go and stay with you or did some of them stay back in school, or what was the situation with that?

Well, no. Some of these fellas didn't make music their career, and I had to wind up, with the exception of my banjo player who was Talcott Reeves. He's in New York now, and he's the Vice President of a Butcher's Association there. He doesn't play any more. But that little guy was great though. He was one of the originals, from Fort Smith, Arkansas. Talcott Reeves. He was (inaudible). went to school with me. We went to New York. The McCord brothers, Theodore and Castor, went to New York. And these are some of the guys that played the Savoy Ballroom, the Dunbar Palace. And of course, I augmented and (inaudible) my band in New York with some of the New York musicians.
